Researchers believe Vincent van Gogh’s The Starry Night may show the sky before dawn on July 22, 1889. Long considered an imagined scene sketched in mid-June at the Saint-Paul-de-Mausole asylum in Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, the painting may instead reflect a real view.

Comparing the sky above Van Gogh’s window with the artwork, researchers found the crescent moon, Venus, and the Hyades star cluster in matching positions. His letters show he explored night-sky ideas in mid-June, while astronomical analysis suggests he completed the painting more than a month later.

The findings reveal how Van Gogh combined observation with his distinctive swirling brushwork.

[Kim et al. (2026), “The actual sky of Van Gogh’s Starry Night: a multidisciplinary reconstruction,” Scientific Reports. DOI: 10.1038/s41598-026-73025-5]

🇧🇷 Flávio Bolsonaro declares himself Brazil's "true president-elect" from the US

Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who lost Sunday's presidential runoff to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva by about 4.4 million votes, has published a letter from the United States calling himself "the true president-elect of Brazil."

He claims the election was stolen, pointing in particular to the Supreme Court decision that extended voting by two hours on election day, and says those responsible are a criminal organization that has imposed a tyranny on Brazil. He offered no evidence, and both campaigns, his own included, had asked for that extension. His own Liberal Party has already accepted the result.

Bolsonaro left Brazil with his family on Tuesday in defiance of a Supreme Court order to surrender his passports, crossing into Argentina before flying to Miami. The Trump administration has granted the family visas. He is under investigation for corruption and money laundering, which he denies, and says he left over fears of political persecution. He vowed to lead the opposition from abroad.

In the letter, he thanked Argentine President Javier Milei for his "courage, sense of justice and respect for legality," and US President Donald Trump and "the wonderful American people" for taking him in.

"I did not flee Brazil. I left for Brazil's sake," he wrote, comparing himself to Charles de Gaulle, who led Free France from London after being sentenced to death by the Vichy regime.
